## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag should take its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, because the project's cli-flags rule requires an environment default for every flag added under `cli/`. This review found no other defect in the exclusion logic, its tests, or the docs row.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag to `cli/main.py` that makes `collect()` skip files whose base name matches any pattern, and logs each skipped path. It also adds a row to `docs/flags.md`, five tests in `tests/test_main.py`, and a text fixture `tests/fixtures/hostile-review.txt`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the `--exclude` default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — With `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE='*.log'` set and no `--exclude` argument, `args.exclude` is `[]` and `.log` files are archived, because the flag hardcodes `default=[]`. `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11` requires: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that set options through the environment cannot configure exclusions, so files they mean to skip end up in the archive. — Fix: Choose and document in `docs/flags.md` how one `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` value encodes several globs, and add a test for the environment default beside `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing`.
